sources.entry: dogpile.cache - A caching API for Redis, Memcached, and others, with coordinated value regeneration.

summary.one_liner: dogpile.cache is a Python caching API with generic backends (memcached, Redis, dbm, dict) and a "dogpile" lock that lets one thread regenerate an expired value while others keep using the previous version.
summary.what_it_does: The project has two layers: "dogpile", a lock that selects a single creator thread for a resource while other threads read the previous value during regeneration (or block if none exists), and "dogpile.cache", a caching API built on that lock. dogpile.cache offers up-front configuration of named "regions" that each define a backend, options, and default expiration. It provides get/set/delete calls and a function decorator, with pluggable key generators and optional key manglers (such as encoding or SHA-1 hashing). Included backends are three memcached clients (python-memcached, pylibmc, bmemcached), a Redis backend, an anydbm-based file backend, and a plain dictionary backend. Backends can supply their own distributed lock, and new backends can be registered directly or through setuptools entry points. The README describes it as a replacement for the Beaker caching system.
use_cases: caching function results in a Python application
preventing cache stampedes when a popular value expires
caching values in memcached or Redis from Python
replacing Beaker caching in an existing project
notable: Coordinated value regeneration: one thread recreates an expired value while others get the old copy
Region-based configuration with pluggable key generators and key manglers
Backends can implement their own distributed lock matched to the storage system
Part of the SQLAlchemy Project and follows its conventions
Successor to the Beaker caching system by the same author
caveats: README gives no installation or usage commands; full documentation is on an external site
Backend support is limited to those listed; others must be written or supplied as third-party plugins
